Independent Study

Independent study with Professor Emiliano Dall'Anese and Ph.D student Damola Ajeyemi investigating stability boundaries of renewable integrated electrical grid

Status: In progress

Tools: Julia, Modeling and Simulation

Independent Study

Problem Statement

As more renewable resources are integrated into the electrical grid, the control models which previously relied on characteristics of synchronous generators must be reevaluated to ensure continued stability of the system. My goal will be to construct grid systems of interest and to develop tests which evaluate selected control models and parameters.

Discussion of Prior Work

The electrical grid requires a precise balancing of generation and load as well as synchronization of frequency, all of which are stabilized through various control systems. Work by Milano, et al [1] provides background information on the effect of replacing traditional power generation sources with renewable resources on these control systems and presents open questions. Some of the effects and open questions relevant to this Independent Study include; decreased window of time during which a control system must react to stabilize the grid after a disturbance as well as balancing precision and compute in selecting a modeling fidelity. Next, in [2], the focus is on outlining the existing control models for traditional and renewable energy sources. Most importantly, [2] describes a control paradigm that could provide the stability that is lost when traditional power generation sources are replaced with renewable resources and proposes control systems as a unifying tool to integrate the complexities of this system moving forward. Finally, [3] introduces an open-source software package used for running custom simulations to test grid stability.
